points.response: Conceded as to the mechanical elements: F6 records the tap at 12:17:10, 39 m from the pickup (within the data-layer 200 m parameter), so NS-1(i)/(ii) are satisfied on the records — I withdraw any suggestion that the driver failed to press the button or pressed it out of position.

A single in-app message at 12:17 (F9) is not itself a finding of no-show, and the rider's own case is that he was not aware the driver had arrived until he came out; the driver's only other communication is his own 12:25 announcement of cancellation (F10), and the chat contains nothing from the rider agreeing or refusing anything (F11) — so the 'no-show' conclusion rests on the driver's assertion in F12, which under RD-5/G11 is a claim, not consent or proof.

I do not contest record completeness — F11 shows two timestamped messages and F3 shows GPS coverage through cancellation; my point is only that completeness works against the driver too: the complete record shows the rider sent nothing and the driver's 12:25 message announces a cancellation timed to his own 8-minute count (F10), not to any platform threshold stated in the record.

The problem is the label, not the dollar: the $5.00 line (F7) is the published waiting-time charge for NS-6, which requires the trip to continue and the rider to board and the driver to tap the fee button at drop-off, while F4 and F5 record a cancellation at 12:25:20 with no completed trip — a $5.00 item that was not a waiting fee cannot be sustained as one under FARE-1.

NS-2 is not my sole ground; on the policy's own framing the $5.00 charge (F7) fails as an NS-6 waiting fee because no boarding and no completed trip occurred (F4, F5), and the driver's statement applies an '8 minutes the rule gives' clock (F12) that the policy tells us not to substitute for the actual threshold — so the fee is contestable even where NS-1's mechanical elements appear in the driver's favour.

I accept the driver's history cannot decide the case (F16, F17) and I press F17 only as a support for account review, not as proof; but 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F17) is precisely the 'repeated' pattern RD-6 contemplates when added to this fee-basis dispute, whereas the driver's 824 trips and account age (F17) are irrelevant to whether this particular $5.00 charge was sustainable.

C1 proves my case rather than the rider's: it concedes the tap at 12:17:10 was 39 m from the pickup (F6) and that the driver stayed within 200 m for 8 min 10 s after the tap (F6) while stationary 12:16:50–12:25:20 at 41 m (F3), which is exactly the (i)(ii)(iii) combination NS-1 requires, so no_action — not fee_waived — follows.

C2 mis-uses the driver's plain wording: NS-1 does not require a 8-minute threshold, and each measurement the system records meets it — the tap-to-cancellation wait of 8 min 10 s (F6) exceeds the > 3-minute requirement, and the arrival-to-cancellation gap of 9 min 55 s (F5) does too, so the fee is earned on either clock; the "8 minutes" in F10/F12 is the free-wait figure the policy tells us not to substitute, not a rejected threshold.

C3 attacks a charge nobody made: the $5.00 on record (F7) is a published waiting/cancellation charge under Ryde's fee schedule and no unpublished item appears, since the surge multiplier is 1.0x (F8), so FARE-1 has nothing to strip out — FARE-1 only refunds items that are unpublished or that fail their own clause.

C4's rider-silence point cuts against the rider: NS-1 turns on the driver's records and the rider's failure to board, not on the rider's consent, and the complete timestamped chat (F11) shows the driver gave notice at 12:17 (F9) and cancelled only after the wait — a wait during which no rider message of any kind appears in the two-message record.

C5 is irrelevant, not adverse: nothing in NS-1 conditions the fee on traffic weather or congestion, and the driver never relied on a reroute justification, so the absence of incidents (F14) and the fair weather (F15) simply confirm an unobstructed pickup that the rider did not attend.

C6's own framing concedes profile facts cannot prove the charge wrong, and RD-6's flag is available only where the underlying breach is established; here the mechanical records satisfy NS-1 (F3, F6), so there is no established violation to attach a flag to, and the driver does not seek one.

Standing by D1: the tap position of 39 m at 12:17:10 (F6) is inside the arrival radius and the closest approach of 6 m at 12:16:45 (F1) confirms the driver was physically at the pickup point, satisfying NS-1(i)–(ii).

Clarifying D5: the $5.00 (F7) is the published waiting-time charge and, with no surge (F8), no unpublished add-on exists for FARE-1 to refund; the fee stands on the NS-1 predicate that a driver pressed "I'm Here" and waited beyond 3 minutes, which F6 and F3 establish.
